_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY - a shape reference, not content. The prices and items below exist to show one of
each schema feature; what a run's shop actually sells, and what it costs, is server content and
a balance decision (plan §2.7 keeps transcribed content out of the mod entirely).
Write your own at data/<your-namespace>/roguelite/shop_tables/<name>.json, or shadow this path
from your own datapack to delete this example.
Any field whose name starts with '_' is ignored, which is where comments go. Every other unknown
field is an error, so a typo is reported instead of silently taking a default.
_this_is_the_PAID_half: The between-wave step has TWO halves and this file is only the second one.
1. THREE FREE OPTIONS, one of which the player takes. Random, rarity-tiered, rerollable for
credits. Those come from a REWARD table (reward_tables/*.json), not from here - see
RewardOffer. Nothing in this file is free and nothing in it is picked one-of.
2. THIS: a short row of ordinary consumables, ALWAYS THE SAME ONES, priced, bought as often
as the player can afford. See ShopStock.
The split is the feel of the step. The free pick is a choice under scarcity - three doors, one
key. This row is PLANNING: the Revive is always there, so a player can skip a purchase now and
save for it. A shop that randomised its stock could not be planned against and would just be a
worse copy of the free offer.
So there is NO random draw here, no seed and nothing to reroll: stock is the eligible entries in
AUTHORED ORDER, capped at the wave's slot count. Order matters - re-sorting would make the row
look random even with fixed contents.
Two things do change with depth. Prices rise (see price_curve below), and the row GETS LONGER -
three consumables early, five later. How many is mechanism, not content: ShopRules.shopSlots.
There are no TIERS here, unlike reward_tables. Tiers exist so rarity can ramp with depth; this
_entries: 'reward' is the SAME object the reward tables take - see RunReward, whose sealed list is §2.12's
boundary on what a reward can be. A datapack can add entries, prices and whole tables; it cannot
add a KIND of reward, because there would be no code to apply it.
'price' is authored per entry and never derived. A formula from reward magnitude to cost would be
wrong in both directions at once: 10 Attack EVs and 10 HP EVs cost the same to compute and are
worth wildly different amounts, and the same item is a bargain at wave 20 and a rounding error at
'weight' is relative likelihood among entries eligible at that wave; it says nothing about depth.
Weight 0 shelves an entry without deleting it, and is reported at load so it is not a surprise.
'min_wave'/'max_wave' are a HARD content rule ('no ability patch before wave 40'), separate from
pricing on purpose - a rebalance of prices should not reopen content that was closed deliberately.
'price_curve' scales 'price' as a PERCENTAGE at that wave: 100 is the authored price, 300 triple.
It exists because credits-per-wave grows with depth (CreditRules), so a flat price becomes free by
the late run. Reuses the reward tables' curve format rather than inventing a second one.

entries._note: The cheap staple, always stocked. Weight is unused by this half and may be omitted.
Held item, mid-run onward. Weight left at its default of 1.

_note: Late-run power purchase that gets more expensive as credits inflate. Triples in price between
wave 40 and wave 200, which roughly tracks the earn curve rather than outrunning it.

entries._note: An early-only entry, closed off once the run is past the point it would matter.
